pr_body:
Fix the thread function signatures to match k_thread_entry_t. This won't make a real difference in most cases, as the threads won't return anyway. But theoretically this could cause a stack corruption.

Fixes #62637
pr_comments:
So far I have not dealt with the unused arguments, as I am uncertain which is the current way to go. Mostly I have seen ARG_UNUSED, but according to #26978 __unused is available and used as well.

There are >100 other cases of this issue as well, this PR covers only zephyr/drivers/** by now.

issue_context.title: Incorrect function signature for ADC data acquisition threads
issue_context.body:
Data acquisition threads for ADCs usually have the incorrect function signature. Examples are:

- https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/94cc1bf4551a933200f1f65777a19869264bc5bf/drivers/adc/adc_ads1119.c#L436
- https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/94cc1bf4551a933200f1f65777a19869264bc5bf/drivers/adc/adc_ads114s0x.c#L1066
- https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/94cc1bf4551a933200f1f65777a19869264bc5bf/drivers/adc/adc_ads1x1x.c#L540
- https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/94cc1bf4551a933200f1f65777a19869264bc5bf/drivers/adc/adc_ads7052.c#L222

They all have one parameter, but the thread entry function pointer is defined as:

    typedef void (*k_thread_entry_t)(void *p1, void *p2, void *p3);

Therefore these functions would corrupt the stack if they would return, which they luckily won't ever do.

I'm uncertain if this is intended, but I wanted to at least mentioned this imperfection.
comments: @benediktibk would you be better off opening a PR to fix the functions if you have a chance?

review_comments: This change failed to update the actual implementation of `alternate_thread()` to have the correct signature. It's now causing CI failures for other PRs.
Sorry for that, but I am really curious why it then passed the CI for this PR. Any ideas?
The PR CI and push CI run two different set of tests, and then the weekly run is a much wider set so even after the push and PR there may be some leftover warning.

In which case is the PR and the push CI run? These failures popped up in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/64570, which I assume should run the same tests as this PR?

BTW, I'm already trying to fix it in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/64579

That's the workflow definition: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/.github/workflows/twister.yaml, there's a bunch of branches depending whether it's `push`, `pull_request_target` or `schedule`, the specific implementations are beyond me but the PR one does something based the modified files I think and the schedule one is a monster run with all possible combination I think (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/actions/workflows/twister.yaml?query=event%3Aschedule).
